ADANIPOWER.title: Dispatch improved, but prior-period recoveries and tax credit amplify headline profit
ADANIPOWER.summary: Power sales rose 11.5% to 26.4 billion units and continuing EBITDA reached ₹6,321 crore. Reported EBITDA of ₹8,743 crore includes ₹2,422 crore net prior-period revenue, while PAT of ₹7,019 crore also benefits from a tax credit. Mahan commissioning moved to early FY28; normalization and cash-history gaps remain unscored.
drivers: Power volumes and PLF rose. Continuing PPA realization grew 12.7%, supported by tariff indexation and additional medium-term contracts.
Higher imported coal prices raise fuel cost and tariffs. Bangladesh pass-through is immediate, while Gujarat indexation lags more than six months.
Reported-to-continuing EBITDA and PBT differences both tie to ₹2,422 crore net prior-period revenue. This is not all new recurring earning power.
risks: Management expects normal thermal PLF around 65%, below this quarter’s 70.1%; weak hydro availability is not a permanent tailwind.
Mahan 1.6 GW commercial operations now target early FY28, later than the archived FY27 / Q2 FY27 timing.
Korba’s second 660 MW unit has conflicting timing: opening remarks say Q4 FY27, while Q&A says around December. No version is selected without clarification.
The Haryana compensation claim was reversed despite cash receipt. The settlement and potential interest remain uncertain.
Gross debt grew while net debt was broadly stable with additional cash balances. Peak-debt guidance around ₹1 lakh crore by FY30/31 needs funding and debt-service checks.
next: Obtain project-specific commercial operation dates, especially Mahan and both Korba units.
Reconcile gross prior-period claims, net prior-period revenue, the Haryana reversal and current/prior tax without double counting.
Track continuing EBITDA per unit sold, fuel cost and PPA realization on matched scopes; do not annualize a high-PLF quarter mechanically.
Reconcile filed H1 CFO, capex and cash with ₹61,860 crore gross debt and ₹45,846 crore net debt.
guidance: Normal thermal-project PLF expectation is around 65%; current dispatch benefited from low hydro availability.
Mahan Phase II 1,600 MW commercial operations target early FY28.
Korba’s first 660 MW unit should operate in Q3. Second-unit opening remarks say Q4 FY27, while Q&A says around December; both versions are retained.
Capacity target is 45 GW by 2032: 42 GW organic plus 3 GW acquisitions.
Peak debt is expected around ₹1 lakh crore by FY30 or FY31.

ASTERDM.title: Merged platform expands occupancy and EBITDA; statutory YoY is explicitly non-comparable
ASTERDM.summary: Management reports combined like-for-like Q2 revenue growth19% and operating EBITDA growth25%, with occupancy68% and realised synergiesINR16.6crore. Limited-review prior periods were not restated after the1July merger effective date, so statutory growth cannot be read as organic improvement. Management-adjusted PAT, seasonal margins and cash-flow quality remain separate unresolved checks.
drivers: Combined patients served rose12% and occupied beds8% against operational-bed growth4%; occupancy improved335bps to68%.
More complex care, mature-unit operating leverage and integrated procurement/talent synergies support management-defined EBITDA.
Q2 realised synergiesINR16.6crore equal an approximatelyINR65crore annualised run-rate; neither is the full futureINR200crore realised benefit.
risks: Statutory current/prior scopes differ because Quality Care enters limited-review statements only from1July2026; management comparatives use proforma Quality Care.
Q2 benefited from seasonal medical/dengue cases; management rejects treating24% quarterly margin as the full-year baseline.
Expansion includes greenfields and material funding needs; net debt/TTMEBITDA is0.87× excluding leases but1.72× including leases.
Management normalised PAT is not reconciled here to statutory current/prior attributablePAT; no CFO or current absoluteARPOB series is disclosed.
next: Reconcile audited combined comparable periods, statutory-to-management EBITDA/PAT and weighted share-count effects.
Track occupancy, occupied bed days, patient mix/ARPOB and mature/emerging fixed cohorts with matched definitions.
Separate quarterly realised synergies, annualised run-rate and full realised savings over the promised four- versus six/seven-quarter horizons.
Verify project-level capex, funded bed additions, unit breakevens, lease-adjusted leverage and H1CFO.
guidance: Full INR200crore synergy run-rate expected by about the fourth quarter; full realised number by the sixth or seventh quarter.
Full-year operating margin target24–25% in two to three years post-merger, including greenfield/brownfield expansion; Q2 is not the recurring base.
4230 additional bed pipeline on10840 total capacity, with47%brownfield/53%greenfield;454-bedTrivandrum inFY27 plan.

BEL.title: Execution accelerated, but order replenishment still depends on unsigned programmes
BEL.summary: BEL reports H1 revenue growth of 25.97% and PAT growth of 14.80%, with 27.43% EBITDA margin. Management attributes part of the fast first-half growth to smoother quarterly production and retains its full-year growth range. The ₹68,717 crore October 1 backlog remains substantial, but ₹7,334 crore H1 intake trails deliveries. QRSAM and BEL NGC suborders remain prospective; NGC must not be added twice to inflow guidance.
drivers: H1 revenue ₹12,824 crore and PAT ₹2,589 crore establish fast execution with slower profit conversion, not pure margin-led growth.
Management is deliberately distributing production more evenly through the year and advancing committed deliveries; H1 growth is not an upgraded annual run rate.
NGC parent contracts progressed, but BEL expects staggered suborders. Its expected ₹20,000 crore NGC value is already included within the ₹25,000 crore ex-QRSAM guide.
Backlog is diversified across electronics, aircraft, missile systems, upgrades, radar and export orders; its components are subsets of the total, not incremental revenue.
risks: QRSAM remained unsigned after the prior September expectation; procurement/negotiation delays can shift inflow and execution.
H1 orders acquired are below H1 revenue; a large backlog alone does not prove replenishment.
H1 financial remarks do not explicitly name accounting view; keep them distinct from frozen consolidated rows until reconciled.
Current call contains no receivables, statutory H1 CFO, customer-advance balance or cash-conversion bridge.
Mid-call ₹55,000 crore total-inflow guide differs from closing ₹50,000-plus wording; do not silently select the more favorable value.
Proactive QRSAM production-model/supply-chain investment precedes a firm award; financial exposure and customer advances are not quantified.
next: Confirm QRSAM signed award, final value, advance terms and delivery schedule rather than an expected approval date.
Track dated NGC BEL purchase orders and remove any double counting versus the ex-QRSAM base.
Reconcile Q2-only operating margin and H1 accounting basis; test annual approximately 28% EBITDA-margin guidance.
Collect matched H1 CFO, receivables, customer advances, inventories and capex before assessing cash quality.
Recalculate book-to-bill and backlog/revenue on a frozen same-scope denominator; near-2.5x ratios are sensitive to view and timing.
guidance: FY27 revenue growth remains more than 15%, with 15–20% planning range; high H1 growth partly reflects more uniform quarterly production, not a guidance upgrade.
FY27 order inflow ₹25,000 crore excluding QRSAM and ₹55,000 crore including QRSAM reiterated mid-call. NGC anticipated ₹20,000 crore is included in the ex-QRSAM base, not additional.
Closing guidance says ₹25,000 crore minimum excluding QRSAM and ₹50,000-plus crore including it, differing from ₹55,000 crore earlier. Preserve wording conflict.
Approximately 28% EBITDA margin, ₹2,200-plus crore R&D investment, approximately ₹1,200 crore capex and typically 90:10 defence/nondefence mix. These are guidance, not H1 actuals.
NGC BEL suborders expected over one day to six months; most expected before March, but some line items may slip to April. Typical execution around 3–4 years after firm orders.

BHARTIARTL.title: ARPU and cash generation improved; fibre correction and new growth capex qualify the extrapolation
BHARTIARTL.summary: India mobile ARPU rose to ₹271 from ₹264, helped by mix, a Q2 prepaid-ladder intervention and one extra day. Record source-reported postpaid additions and more than 200m 5G users support premiumization. Group EBITDAaL-minus-capex exceeds ₹19,000cr, but this is management operating FCF rather than statutory free cash flow. Homes added 670k amid an acquisition-quality correction and a shift back toward fibre; new data-center/cloud capex and a ₹2,900cr land purchase limit a simple declining-capex narrative. No broad tariff timing, complete cash-capex bridge or analyst-normalized PAT is established.
drivers: Mobile premiumization: 1.2m postpaid adds, 2.9m smartphone-data adds and ₹271 ARPU, with pricing/calendar effects identified rather than called pure volume.
Africa revenue grew 6.7% sequentially at constant currency; preserve this scope and period instead of treating it as YoY or reported FX growth.
India ex-passive EBITDAaL above ₹20,400cr and 52.7% margin support operating cash capacity, while core radio capex has moderated.
Homes is switching toward fibre-led, higher-quality acquisition; current net adds, ARPU and EBIT reflect a correction rather than an unqualified acceleration.
risks: Pricing intervention temporarily affects customer continuity; broad industry data monetization remains unresolved and no tariff date is promised.
Homes low-ARPU/wrong-sales-practice correction and additional fibre/CPE investment can keep EBIT soft before customer quality improves.
Nxtra/cloud build-out is lumpy; land acquisition and possible future debt/equity funding can absorb operating cash.
Africa currency exposure and NBFC credit/capital returns are not resolved by strong revenue or loan-disbursement run rates.
next: Decompose next-quarter ARPU into calendar, targeted pack changes and mix; compare churn and revenue-earning additions.
Track homes net adds, retention, ARPU and EBIT following the fibre pivot, with comparable customer-quality definitions.
Reconcile cash capex, capitalization, CWIP and separate land spending to statutory cash flow, then debt and dividends.
For Nxtra separate land optionality, under-construction and commissioned MW; for NBFC separate disbursements, revenue, credit losses and deployed equity.
guidance: Management sees sustained ARPU growth from upgrades, postpaid, roaming and top-ups; Q2 prepaid-ladder pricing intervention has already played out. No date or amount of industry-wide tariff hike is guided.
Nxtra aims for one gigawatt over the next few years; the newly acquired land provides 400–500MW optionality over time, with lumpy data-center build expenditure over 12–18 months.
Core capex broadly consistent; incremental investments go toward data centers and cloud. Dividend payouts are intended to increase over time.
Gross debt directionally comes down subject to operations and dividend outflows; current tax provision/payment run rates can be used going forward.
Homes is an investment phase; management wants to accelerate quality customer additions through fiber while correcting low-quality/low-ARPU acquisitions.

adj.item: One extra calendar day in mobile ARPU

DIVISLAB.title: CS mix and backward integration lift profits; approvals and working capital still qualify conversion
DIVISLAB.summary: H1 standalone constant-currency revenue grew 17%, while consolidated Q2 PAT rose to ₹1,127 crore from ₹689 crore. Management attributes the lower material-consumption ratio to CS mix and backward integration. The new dedicated projects remain approval-dependent, and rising inventories/receivables prevent treating profit growth as confirmed cash conversion.
drivers: CS contributes 62% of H1 sales; the source does not quantify validation-batch revenue or recurring base-business margin.
Net material consumption falls to approximately 32% of sales from 40%, with management citing CS mix and Kakinada backward integration rather than lower input prices.
Older CS programs already commercialize; one new dedicated project is described as very close to commercialization and the other two are expected over the next one or two quarters.
Peptide investment is customer-specific innovator work; management explicitly says it does not currently make generic peptides.
risks: Dedicated-project and peptide approvals, customer qualification and commercial economics remain undisclosed; no named-product opportunity is verified.
Inventory ₹5,325 crore and receivables ₹3,705 crore coexist with a three-month critical-material buffer and elevated solvent/logistics costs.
The analyst cites weaker pre-tax operating cash, but management answers with capex/CWIP; this does not reconcile the operating-cash bridge.
Management reiterates double-digit revenue growth but declines to commit to sustaining the 40%+ EBITDA margins raised by analysts.
next: Verify customer/agency approval and repeat commercial shipments for the three dedicated investments; resolve archival deadline conflicts first.
Reconcile filed H1 operating cash before/after tax, working-capital changes, capital advances and cash capex rather than equating capitalization with cash spend.
Track like-defined standalone CC revenue, CS mix, consumed-material ratio and recurring margins after validation-batch mix normalizes.
Require disclosed customer concentration and product economics before treating peptide capability as a quantified earnings stream.
guidance: Double-digit revenue growth remains the forward view; management declines to specify 10%, 17% or 20%.
One dedicated project is very close to commercialization; the other two are expected over the next one or two quarters, subject to customer/agency qualification.
Annual capex planning of approximately ₹2,000 crore plus or minus 20%, based on RFPs, reiterated for the next two to three years.
No upgraded 40%+ EBITDA-margin commitment is given; management repeats only double-digit revenue-growth guidance.

HINDALCO.title: India metals earnings surged, but copper windfalls and pot-relining accounting lift the headline
HINDALCO.summary: India upstream aluminium EBITDA reached ₹7,009 crore with shipments only 1% higher YoY, so its 55% EBITDA increase was principally a pricing/premium and profitability result rather than a volume surge. Downstream EBITDA grew 26% to ₹329 crore on 6% shipment growth. Copper EBITDA of ₹1,673 crore includes approximately ₹350–400 crore of management-identified nonrepeatable gains, and the suggested ₹1,200–1,300 crore future run rate still assumes unusually high sulfuric-acid prices. Capitalizing pot relining raises EBITDA and depreciation by roughly the same ₹130 crore ongoing amount; this is a presentation/comparability change, not the same amount of incremental PAT. Novelis recovery and deleveraging remain forward execution tests.
drivers: India upstream: shipments rose 1% and revenue 33% YoY; higher net export premiums and value-added upstream-product pricing supported EBITDA/t of $2,125 despite a 5% sequential cost increase (PDF pp. 6, 9, 12).
India downstream: 119 kt shipments, up 6%, and ₹329 crore EBITDA versus ₹261 crore; management attributes the stronger earnings conversion to product mix and premiumization (PDF pp. 6–7).
Copper: 116 kt shipments (+2%) and 96 kt CCR volumes (stable), while by-product pricing, precious-metal sales and temporary gains magnified the EBITDA increase (PDF pp. 7, 9, 12, 15).

Novelis: Oswego hot-mill production is described as normalized, with $519 million cumulative insurance recoveries through September; Bay Minette first coil is a milestone preceding commercial shipments, which are now expected in Q1 FY28 (PDF p. 7).
risks: The ₹1,200–1,300 crore copper run-rate expectation assumes sulfuric acid at ₹14,000–15,000/tonne, well above the roughly ₹3,000–4,000 historical reference cited by management; this is cyclical operating profit, not assured normalized earnings (PDF pp. 9, 13).

India upstream production costs rose roughly 5% QoQ and management expects a further roughly 5% increase in Q3; coal availability and CP coke prices limit an immediate cost-down interpretation (PDF pp. 9, 15).
Higher Q3 aluminium costs coincide with export/MJP premiums retreating by more than $100; premium and mix benefits should not both be assumed permanent (PDF p. 16).
Novelis still faces tariff, customer-supply-chain and Yeongju strike effects; an indicated $20 million strike effect in Q2 is expected again in Q3 (PDF p. 10).

India expansion capex and execution capacity are constraints, while the consolidated leverage target is around 2x and Novelis is guided toward roughly 4x at Q4 before later deleveraging (PDF pp. 8, 11, 17).
next: Reconcile quarterly India upstream EBITDA on a constant pot-relining policy and isolate the unspecified Q1 catch-up recorded in Q2.

Track copper EBITDA after the ₹350–400 crore temporary gains, sulfuric-acid realization and the premium/by-product contribution; compare against the conditional ₹1,200–1,300 crore management run rate.
Check Q3 aluminium cost/tonne, export premiums and Aditya FRP product qualifications; management expects downstream EBITDA/t to cross $300 as products qualify.
Confirm Bay Minette commercial shipments in Q1 FY28 and separately follow ramp-up, capex, customer qualification and cash generation rather than treating first coil as full commissioning.
Obtain scope-matched Novelis H1 EBITDA/t excluding tariff and quarterly debt/cash statements before assessing the archived $480/t H1 and consecutive-quarter leverage gates.
guidance: Novelis long-term EBITDA/t guidance of $600 remains unchanged; positive free cash flow and the beginning of deleveraging are expected by end FY27.
Bay Minette produced first cold-rolled coil in September 2026; commercial shipments expected Q1 FY28.
Pakhajan copper recycling commissions December 2026; Aditya alumina refinery and first 180kt smelter line December 2027; second smelter line and copper smelter December 2028.
Aluminium cost expected roughly 5% higher Q3 versus Q2, with relief anticipated in Q4. Bandha first coal in H2 of next financial year and Chakla around middle of next year.
Copper quarterly EBITDA run rate around ₹1,200–1,300 crore assumes sulfuric-acid realization around ₹14,000–15,000/t in Q3/Q4.

obs.m: India upstream aluminium EBITDA per tonne

obs.cl: prior-year quarter; continuation on PDF p.7

IKS.title: Acquisition doubles reported revenue; legacy growth and cash definitions temper the print
IKS.summary: Reported rupee revenue growth of about 104% includes 82 days of TruBridge, while legacy IKS USD growth is only a little above 13%. Legacy margins remain healthy, but most integration synergies lie ahead. Management-adjusted OCF excludes acquisition cash; future growth and margin targets remain ambitions.
drivers: TruBridge adds about USD68 million of acquired revenue; legacy IKS contributes about USD101 million and grows a little above 13% in USD terms.
Legacy IKS including AQuity sustains approximately 34.5–35% EBITDA margin; acquired scope lowers the combined reported margin to about 28%.
Four legacy wins include Augusta Health cross-sell, White-Wilson, Evolve and UMass Memorial; commercial ramp amounts remain undisclosed.
Management sees data and cross-sell opportunity in the acquired EHR base but says bulk synergies have not yet been realized.
risks: Reported growth is heavily inorganic; no significant net TruBridge growth is expected in FY27.
Integration expenses, debt interest, intangible amortization and prospective ESOP dilution create distinct shareholder costs.
Customer stabilization, lumpy short-term projects and AI-related price compression qualify recurring growth.
A full-quarter acquisition comparison, exact EHR customer counts, statutory cash bridge and current comparable revenue/FTE history remain missing.
next: Reconcile a full quarter of reported, organic/CC and acquired revenue plus named-client ramps.
Track realized TruBridge synergies from the second half of Q3 and launch of three features by Q1 FY28.
Bridge reported OCF to management-adjusted OCF, including the acquisition cash classification and tax timing, rather than treating adjusted cash as H1 CFO.
Measure net leverage, interest, intangible amortization and the announced roughly 4% ESOP grant against the FY30 ambition.
guidance: Legacy IKS ambition is to grow faster than management’s 12% industry benchmark; management explicitly says growth expectations are ambitions, not formal guidance.

No significant TruBridge net growth expected in FY27; system-of-action growth intended to build in FY28 and approach 10–12% late FY28/early FY29. EHR system-of-record book is intended to remain relatively flat.
Three features targeted for integration into the legacy TruBridge EHR by Q1 FY28.
INR3000 crore FY30 EBITDA True North and near-zero net leverage by FY30 remain management ambitions, not achieved outcomes.
Early-to-mid-30s margin aspiration for both books by FY30; no specific FY28/FY29 margin guidance provided.

INDIGO.title: Narrower reported loss masks weaker like-for-like economics as the domestic fuel cap expires
INDIGO.summary: IndiGo reported a consolidated INR19bn quarterly loss versus INR26bn last year, but management ex-MTM/hedging result deteriorated from INR1bn profit to about INR7bn loss. PRASK rose31%, yet fuelCASK rose69% and nonfuel/nonforex-MTM CASK rose15%. Domestic fuel-cap protection ended June8. Capacity is being rationalized and damp-leased widebody operations end November1; freecash balance remains INR399bn. This is a cost-and-liquidity case, not a clean earnings-recovery winner.
drivers: PRASK +31% and yield growth >34% partly compensate for elevated jet-fuel costs; load factor fell about2pp, so stronger sales are not evidence of volume growth.
Fuel CASK +69%; Singapore jet index +60% plus currency effects. Management says the domestic cap ended June8 and fuel purchases are now market-linked.
Nonfuel/nonforex-MTM CASK INR3.45/ASK, +15%, reflects actual dollar-linked expense inflation, lower utilization and contractual escalations.
Damp-lease exit is expected to improve spreads but no numerical contribution is given. Management retains fleet orders/A3502028 and long-term growth guidance.
Ancillary revenue per passenger increased from about INR525 to590; loyalty approaches20m members, but monetization/active-member economics remain unquantified.
risks: High jet-fuel crack spreads and rupee depreciation can exceed revenue repricing; fuel and FX are ongoing business risks, not automatically nonrecurring.
Capacity cuts reduce fixed-cost absorption; fiscal2027 early-single-digit growth implies a difficult near-term scaling path despite aircraft deliveries.
Freecash is a balance measure, not H1CFO or net cash after lease obligations; totalcash includes restrictedcash.
Reported-margin comparison is affected by MTM and hedging. Management-defined ex-MTM/hedging PAT needs a statutory bridge.
Premium/loyalty revenues are early-stage; CEO says current premium contribution to yield was not meaningful.
next: Q3FY27: compare actualPRASK with >25% growth guidance, load factor with flatYoY outlook, and physicalASK growth with early-single-digit guidance.
Reconcile next-quarter ex-MTM/hedging loss/profit and unit spreads after the November1 damp-lease exit; keep FX cash costs separate from remeasurement.
Obtain H1CFO, leasecash payments, financing/debt obligations and FXhedges to assess cash resilience beyond the INR399bn freecash balance.
Verify current engineAOG and revised delivery dates; do not infer airworthy capacity from closingfleet count.
Track activeBluChip participation and incremental ancillary/premium contribution against their investment costs.
guidance: Q3FY27 capacity growth early single digitsYoY; PRASK growth more than25%YoY.
Q3FY27 load factors expected flatYoY based on current bookings.
FY27 capacity growth early single digits; CASK exfuel exforexMTM growth highsingle digits to earlydouble digits.
FY28 growth guidance midteens remains unchanged, subject to review.
CEO retains long-term guidance when asked about300bnASK byFY30, without providing a revised annual bridge.

INFY.title: AI and deal milestones arrived, but the near-term growth thesis weakened
INFY.summary: Infosys reports AI revenue at 10.5% of sales and 29% sequential growth, alongside $5.2 billion of large-deal TCV with 62% net new. Yet Q2 constant-currency growth is only 1.5% YoY and 1.2% QoQ, includes an acquisition contribution, and FY27 constant-currency guidance is cut to 1–2%. The net-new mega deal mainly supports FY28 rather than this year. EBIT margin holds at 21% and quarterly FCF is $928 million, but pricing and volume softness challenge an immediate growth or margin rebound.
drivers: Management attributes the guidance cut to softer volumes, failed expected pricing increases and weaker discretionary spending in Retail/Hi-Tech; offshoring and the European manufacturing client remain separate annual headwinds.
AI adoption is evidenced by management-defined revenue share and growth; it does not establish separate AI profitability or eliminate deflation in the existing portfolio.
Signed TCV and 62% net-new share support pipeline depth, but the main new mega deal transitions only later Q4 and targets FY28 growth contribution.
Maximus 20bps, currency 40bps and workingdays 20bps offset customer-support/acquisition effects; additional realization pressure offsets priorprogram normalization.
QuarterFCF 113% ofnet profit, DSO 64 daysand reported debt-free cash position support current cash discipline; they are not a reconstructed H1 CFO series.
risks: Pricing competition and productivity pass-through can absorb AI growth; management supplies no complete organic AI -versus-legacy revenue bridge.
H2 contains wage hikes, seasonality, acquisition amortization and ramp-up effects; utilization optimization has limited headroom and source definitions need correction.
Deal concentration and conversion timing mean strong TCV need not produce near-term CC growth.
The current transcript does not resolve the prior CEO -succession claim or independently prove current valuation/upside.
next: Track organic CC growth separately from the disclosed~ 0.4pp acquisition contribution; test the revised FY27 range.
Reconcile large-deal transition timing and FY28 recognized revenue, avoiding annualized TCV.
Obtain corrected utilization definitions and matching AI classification; test realized pricing and incremental profit after full costs.
Reconcile management EPS ₹19.32 with frozen ₹19.28 before combining them; preserve the frozen statements pending resolution.
guidance: FY27 revenue growth guidance revised to 1–2% YoY constantcurrency, from the prior 1.5–3% range disclosed in media Q&A.
FY27 operating-margin guidance remains 20–22%; H2 headwinds include compensation, seasonality, AI productivity sharing and large-deal ramp-up.
Net-new $2bn-plus seven-year deal transitions in the second half of Q4 and is expected to contribute over 1% growth in FY28.
Approximately 20,000 freshers target for FY27; about 13,000 hired in H1.
Compensation rollout largely effectiveOctober 2026, with nextphaseJanuary 2027;year tax rate expected 29–30%.

IOC.title: Inventory gains qualify the largest reported earnings addition
IOC.summary: Management identified INR6948 crore of combined refining and marketing inventory gains. Throughput and marketing volumes grew year on year, while refinery throughput declined sequentially. Inventory-neutral recurring profit and an attributable-PAT bridge remain unresolved.
drivers: Physical refining and marketing activity improved year on year.
Inventory gains and diversified gas/petrochemical contributions supported profitability.
Borrowings fell sequentially in the call scope; this is not a reconciled consolidated cash-flow statement.
risks: Inventory gains can reverse with prices.
Marketing and LPG losses, freight and sourcing conditions can offset refining benefits.
Refinery commissioning and throughput ramp-up have different dates; future renewable spending adds funding demands.
next: Reconcile inventory-neutral refining and marketing earnings.
Verify actual refinery commissioning and subsequent throughput.
Match debt, capex, cash and current-period government receivables.
guidance: FY27 budgeted capex INR32700 crore; H1 spend is not annualized.
Panipat, Gujarat and Barauni commissioning targeted during FY27; material throughput ramp-up follows five to six months later.
Terra Clean EBITDA-positive target FY2030; current consolidated cash generation is not inferred.

M&M.title: SUV demand stays strong while tractor outlook and PLI qualify the profit reading
M&M.summary: Capacity-constrained SUV demand and diversified subsidiary profits support the quarter. Tractor industry guidance was cut from +5% to flat FY27. Around INR1000 crore PLI was booked; management says PLI brings current EV margin to about 9%, so sustainable ex-PLI economics remain unproven.
drivers: Management describes strong SUV/LCV demand constrained by capacity; H1 EV mix remains 12%.
Auto/Farm price actions, hedging, mix and operating leverage offset some commodity inflation.
Growth Gems, Mahindra Finance and TechM broaden profit contribution; no monetization occurred this quarter.
International Farm exits are expected to reduce H2 losses and prior exit-cost drag; this is a forward expectation, not a completed profit bridge.
risks: Flat tractor industry outlook and rainfall deficits weaken the old demand-upcycle assumption.
PLI, depreciation and ICE/EV conversion-cost reclassification qualify historical and sustainable-margin comparisons.
New capacity, supplier execution and a later Nagpur plant remain delivery risks.
No full H1 cash-flow/debt/capex bridge or current exact lending credit-quality metrics is provided.

Reconcile PLI recognition, cash receipt, tax/minority effects and EV earnings excluding incentives.
Track delivered capacity versus the February–March EV target and FY27/FY28 plans.
Check core tractor margin, industry inventory and exact subsidiary GS3/NIM/TechM margin goals.
guidance: FY27 tractor industry growth outlook cut from +5% to flattish; this is full-year, not H2 guidance.
Mahindra SUV outlook maintained at mid-to-high teens; LCV industry outlook increased to double digit.
EV monthly capacity expected to increase by around 4000 to 12000 by February–March.
Total Auto capacity plan 82000 per month by FY27 exit, 92000 next year and 132000 by FY31; exact current base differs among oral passages.
Five major launches targeted before end-June 2027.

RELIANCE.title: O2C drives the earnings surge while Retail absorbs online investment
RELIANCE.summary: Management reports consolidated EBITDA ₹62,409cr, up 24%, led by O2C EBITDA ₹25,203cr. Jio customer growth and organic ARPU support digital earnings; Retail revenue grew 6.4% while EBITDA fell as discounts, infrastructure and customer acquisition funded online expansion. The quarter supports refinery flexibility and Jio scale, but weakens a blanket consumer-led mix-improvement narrative. New-energy delivery and cash/return claims remain incompletely evidenced.
drivers: O2C benefited from unusually elevated fuel/product cracks plus crude/product routing, contracted shipping and ethane feedstock flexibility. Management identifies both favorable cyclicality and operational execution; no complete causal rupee bridge is available.
JPL revenue grew 11.4% and EBITDA 16.6%, with 9.1m quarter net additions and ARPU ₹218.8, up 3.5% without a tariff hike. RJIL and JPL scopes remain distinct.

Retail revenue grew 6.4%; grocery walk-in LFL was 3% and consumer-electronics LFL 8%. Online-grocery revenue grew 42%, but discounting, delivery/infrastructure and customer acquisition compressed EBITDA. Management cites festival timing into Q3.
RCPL H1 revenue was ₹16,900cr; revenue expansion does not establish contribution profitability or cash conversion.
risks: High product cracks are cyclical operating benefits; do not annualize the strong quarter into sustainable earnings.
Retail competition remains intense; online mix has lower margins and improvement timing depends on market density and discounting.
New-energy capacity targets and promised FY28 earnings are forward statements, not current operating contributions.
No matching-period H1 CFO reconciliation is established in this single transcript. JPL EBITDA-less-capex wording is internally inconsistent or period-mismatched.
next: Reconcile O2C statutory segment profit, product-crack capture, duties, inventory and feedstock/freight costs.
Track Retail reported EBITDA, pre-charge EBITDA, contribution/order, delivery costs and same-basis quarterly margin.
Verify solar modules/cells/ingot/wafer/polysilicon and BESS/cell commissioning against each original and revised deadline.
Obtain a same-scope H1 cash-flow and net-debt bridge; keep annualized EBITDA forecasts separate from achieved full-year earnings.
guidance: O2C H1 performance tracking annualized EBITDA well over ₹80,000cr; a run-rate expectation, not completed full-year outcome.
Retail investments expected to contribute absolute EBITDA from next year; management retains doubling target but allows one year either side and provides no fixed margin floor.
Solar module capacity targeted up to 20GW early next calendar year; cell capacity to 20GW in first half of next calendar year.
BESS pack/container up to 40GWh and cells around 35–40GWh are prospective; next-half/calendar-year clarification is ambiguous and must not be converted into a precise achieved deadline.
New-energy earnings/revenues expected from FY2028.

SBIN.title: NIM recovery is tangible; the stake-sale gain limits a clean ROA reading
SBIN.summary: SBI reports domestic NIM of 3.11%, low GNPA of 1.39% and a 16.09% capital-adequacy ratio. However, the reported H1 ROA of 1.14% falls to approximately 0.98% in management’s ex-SBI-Funds-stake-sale view. Treasury losses, AFS reserve movements and front-loaded operating expenses affect different lines and must remain separate. The current quarter supports margin recovery and subsidiary monetization while qualifying a blanket claim that underlying ROA is comfortably above 1%.
drivers: Management attributes NIM improvement to higher lending yields, FCNR(B)-funded replacement of wholesale deposits, stronger daily-average current/savings balances, and refusal of unattractively priced T-bill-linked credit (PDF 22).
Corporate credit growth is described as 16% YoY with a roughly ₹7.8 lakh crore pipeline, while bank-wide FY27 credit-growth guidance remains 14-15%; pipeline is not disbursement (PDF 23,25).

SBI Funds monetization contributes to P&L, while NSE divestment/remaining-holding gains are attributed to AFS reserves. Adding the AFS gain to earnings would double count a different accounting location (PDF 9,27).

Operating expenses include approximately ₹850 crore of timing/front-loading, and priority-sector certificate purchases were brought earlier in the year. These are ordinary/timing costs rather than automatically exceptional expenses to add back (PDF 15,16).
risks: Management’s estimated ECL loan transition impact of ₹19,500 crore is after provisions and tax/DTA but explicitly leaves unresolved HTM/crop-loan issues and future recurring earnings volatility. This is management’s prospective scenario, not a verified regulatory rule or booked Q2 charge (PDF 20,21,26).
Potential drought-restructuring portfolio is around ₹10,000 crore; actual uptake is unknown. Agri-gold LTV around 60-61% is not scope-matched to the older overall gold-loan average (PDF 21).
Treasury-loss figures differ within the transcript: ₹1,275 crore on PDF 9 and ₹1,277 crore on PDF 30. This small inconsistency is retained rather than silently resolved.
The call gives no matched SMA2-only growth/PCR history, no full AUCA recovery series, and no six-quarter comparable economic input history; these gaps prevent complete original-plan scoring.
next: Reconcile bank-only and consolidated reported earnings to the SBI Funds stake-sale note, exact after-tax attributable profit and prior-year YES Bank disposal effect.
Track domestic NIM, cost of deposits and lending yields against the unchanged 3% floor; retain actual policy decisions separately from the bank’s December-hike house forecast.
Obtain quarter-specific ROA and core PPOP excluding consistent current/prior disposal items; H1 averages cannot test a two-consecutive-quarter falsification gate.
Monitor corporate disbursements, SMA2, drought restructuring uptake, gross slippages and ECL transition/recurring effects with their own period definitions.
guidance: FY27 bank-wide credit growth remains 14-15%; no next-year guidance supplied.
Domestic NIM not less than 3%; management declines to raise guidance despite described repricing tailwinds.
Annual/through-cycle ROA of 1% and ROE of 15% reiterated.
Overheads target not beyond 10% growth; timing front-loading also planned for Q3.
Management expects/recommends a 50bp December hike and year-end G-sec yield below 7%; these are house forecasts, not realized policy facts.

SOLARINDS.title: Defence execution supports growth; pending orders and cash stay separate
SOLARINDS.summary: Q2 revenue and EBITDA grew with a 29.02% EBITDA margin; defence delivered INR1,002 crore in the quarter. Current defence backlog is INR17,568 crore, while Guided Pinaka remains negotiation. Current domestic physical volume, H1 cash conversion and Omnia closing/financing remain unverified.
drivers: Quarterly revenue INR3,519 crore, EBITDA INR1,021 crore and PAT INR650 crore rose against stated year-earlier amounts.
Defence revenue reached INR1,002 crore in Q2 and INR1,935 crore in H1; management expects FY27 defence sales above INR4,500 crore.
Domestic and international explosives plus defence all contribute, but revenue shares do not isolate physical volume, pricing or currency.
Management attributes domestic performance partly to lower monsoon disruption and demand; no realized domestic volume-growth number is disclosed.
risks: Omnia remains subject to approvals; no new close date, final debt/financing, agricultural economics or realized synergies are provided.
Defence trial-to-contract cycles remain long; Guided Pinaka about INR3,000 crore is not yet booked.
Commodity and supply-chain uncertainty remain; current raw-material expense is not a unit-cost bridge.
No current H1 CFO, working-capital days, capex outturn or debt balance is supplied in this transcript.
next: Verify signed Guided Pinaka orders by FY27 end; keep pending awards outside backlog.
Track Bhargavastra trial completion against calendar 2026 and product-level commercial acceptance.
Reconcile physical domestic volume, realization, mix, FX and acquisitions to reported revenue.
Obtain H1 CFO, inventory/receivables/payables, capex and debt; test cash thresholds without annual backfill.
Confirm Omnia approvals/closing and final financing before crediting synergies.
guidance: Management expects FY27 revenue to exceed INR14,000 crore and defence revenue to exceed INR4,500 crore, without formally replacing guidance because uncertainty remains.
Management expects average full-year EBITDA margin above 29%, versus around 28% initially; this is forward-looking.
Guided Pinaka potential order around INR3,000 crore expected before FY27 end; negotiation is not a signed award.
Bhargavastra internal/field trials targeted in calendar 2026; commercial timing remains uncommitted.
Domestic physical volume growth target around 10–15%; management declines firm FY28/29 guidance and notes outcomes can be flat.

ULTRACEMCO.title: Volumes and operating leverage improve; integration and leverage milestones lag
ULTRACEMCO.summary: Company cement volumes grew 13.8% and utilization rose to 71% from 66%. Lower fixed cost per tonne helps absorb elevated fuel costs, but no organic/acquired growth bridge is disclosed. India Cements EBITDA is only around INR500 per tonne in its own books, below the old INR700 Q2 milestone. Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26 times; below one times by March remains a target.
drivers: Higher company volumes and capacity utilization spread fixed costs: absolute fixed costs rose 4%, while fixed cost per tonne fell 6%.
Domestic capacity reached 204.7 MTPA after September additions; non-fossil power share was 47%.
Management attributes stronger September-exit and October prices to demand/cost conditions; the benefit is expected mainly in Q3, not retroactively in Q2.
Ultravolt launched on 3 September; copper inflation can mechanically increase nominal revenue potential without equivalent unit growth.
risks: Consumed fuel costs are elevated; spot fuel, currency, diesel and domestic coal availability can erode pricing benefits.
India Cements refurbishment and same-entity EBITDA/t remain behind archived near-term milestones.
Net debt/EBITDA rose to 1.26x; capex, dividends and working capital require a current cash bridge.
Company growth is not split into organic versus acquired scope; entity-book and group EBITDA/t are different measures.
Wires-and-cables launch expenses and profitability are not quantified, and INR1100 crore includes commitments rather than all cash spend.
next: Verify like-for-like cement volumes and realized prices, keeping acquired scope separate.
Reconcile consolidated EBITDA/t into price, fuel, fixed cost and integration contributions.
Track India Cements own-books EBITDA/t against the missed INR700 Q2 gate and updated January–March 2028 four-digit target.
Reconcile actual H1 CFO, cash capex, dividends and remaining commitments before testing March leverage below 1x.
Measure Ultravolt secondary sales, unit margins, cash working capital and actual cash capex after the launch.
guidance: FY27 capex remains around INR10000 crore, to be reviewed after Q3; actual H1 spend is not confirmed by management in the cited exchange.
Target net debt/EBITDA below 1x at the end of March FY27; current September ratio is 1.26x.
India Cements four-digit EBITDA/t ambition is now linked to January–March 2028 after kiln/WHRS upgrades.
INR1400/t March 2028 unit-earnings commitment reaffirmed subject to business-as-usual cost/pricing assumptions.
Wires and cables is still ramping; management expects a more mature discussion in April–June 2027 and has not supplied utilization or margin guidance.
